rationale: The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the pattern catalogue (reported VM-time reduction ~12.9% free / ~8.1% paid) and by a measured fork experiment (document experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) showing ~26.8% elapsed savings when adding timeout-minutes: 5 to a comparable Node.js CI job. The repository has representative successful-duration history (multiple successful runs around 22-28 seconds), so a 5-minute bound gives ample headroom without risking valid slow runs, and it bounds runaway consumption without changing any build/test step or coverage. The dependency-cache pattern (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) is not applied because setup-node already declares cache: pnpm, i.e. an equivalent dependency cache already exists, which is a listed contraindication. No permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or new network access is added.
